subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up & next steps (latency / throughput)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Bennett <tbennett@finpay.com>; Priya Kapoor <priya.k@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap and proposed next steps

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Workload: real-time transaction enrichment for fraud scoring ~200 qps peak, 95th percentile latency target <= 120ms for single-request (single-turn) inference.
- Current infra: in-house microservices on AWS, some GPU batch jobs but no dedicated serving layer.
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent PII; they want isolation and long-term audit logs for model inputs.

Given the latency and throughput targets + isolation ask, two viable options we discussed:
1) Redwood Hosted API: fastest to launch, managed scaling, cost-effective for bursty traffic.
   - Pros: quick onboarding, no infra to manage, built-in monitoring and prefix caching.
   - Cons: multitenant isolation (we can offer stronger contract controls but no dedicated GPUs).
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pool, guaranteed throughput & predictable p99 latency, VPC peering available for tighter network controls.
   - Pros: meets tight latency SLOs at scale and provides capacity isolation.
   - Cons: longer lead time for capacity reservation and commitment.

Next steps I recommend:
- Internal sizing: we'll run a quick perf estimate for the model family you plan to serve (you mentioned open-llama-65b quantized) to propose a Dedicated config that meets the 120ms p95/p99 targets at 200 qps.
- Legal/security: share SOC2 scope and network diagram (I've attached the Hosted vs Dedicated comparison and a sample SOW).
- Commercial: if Dedicated is the desired path, I can put together a reserved capacity proposal + SLA options.

Can you confirm: 1) model family and average input size (tokens) for the enrichment call, and 2) whether you need strict tenancy/isolation (Dedicated) for compliance or if contractual controls on Hosted would suffice?

If helpful, we can set a 30-min follow-up next week to review the sizing.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — perf estimate (13B)

Marissa / Vivek — quick estimate based on our recent benchmarks:
- Model: 13B quantized (int8) + Redwood runtime optimizations.
- Single-request p95 (cold) on a single A10-equivalent: ~95ms token generation time for average request (350 in / 50 out). With batching and KV caching for repeated prefixes, steady-state p95 can be brought to ~70-90ms for single-turn requests.
- Throughput: a single 4xA10 pool (4 GPUs) can sustain ~180-220 qps with small batching (batch size 1-4, continuous batching). For 200 qps with 20% burst headroom, recommend a 6-GPU dedicated pool (2x 3-GPU nodes) with autoscale buffer and reserved capacity.
- Network: VPC peering adds ~3-10ms depending on region; recommend colocating Dedicated nodes in the same cloud region as FinPay services.

Recommendation: Dedicated reserved capacity (6 GPUs) with warm pools and autoscale buffers to guarantee p95 <= 120ms at 200 qps. We can also propose a short pilot on Hosted (smaller instance) to validate integration while capacity is being provisioned.

I'll pull together an SLO-aligned cost estimate and a sample reserved capacity quote.

-Neha
